deep.reconstruction:
There is no mathematics on this page. It is a cover or label sheet for a group of folios. It reads: 'Concept der Selbstanzeige der Abhandlung: Beiträge zur Theorie der durch die Gauss'sche Reihe F(α,β,γ,x) darstellbaren Functionen.' In English: 'Draft of the author's own announcement of the treatise: Contributions to the theory of the functions representable by the Gauss series F(α,β,γ,x).' It marks the following material (or the material it is bundled with) as Riemann's draft of the self-review of his 1857 memoir on the hypergeometric function. That memoir appeared in Abh. Kgl. Ges. Wiss. Göttingen 7 (1857). The self-announcement was printed in the Göttinger Nachrichten in 1857 and reprinted in the Gesammelte Werke.

The hand is a neat, regular Kurrent with no corrections, unlike Riemann's working hand on the previous folio. It is very likely a later archival or editorial annotation (for example by Dedekind, Weber, or the Göttingen library) rather than Riemann's own writing; this cannot be settled from the image alone. The folio number '24' in the upper right is an archival foliation.

The context is the previous folio (23). There Riemann works with a conformal map ζ(z), the quantity sqrt(dζ/dz), local exponents 1/4 and 3/4 at points δ, and second-order equations of the form y''/y = Σ c/(ζ-δ)^2. This is P-function / Schwarzian-type material that belongs naturally with the hypergeometric memoir. The cover sheet itself contains no derivation to reconstruct.

results.what: Title/cover note identifying a draft of Riemann's Selbstanzeige (self-announcement) of his memoir on functions representable by Gauss's hypergeometric series F(α,β,γ,x)
results.modern_name: Riemann's 1857 memoir on the hypergeometric function (Riemann P-function, monodromy of the hypergeometric equation)
results.usually_credited_to: Bernhard Riemann (1857); the Selbstanzeige was published in the Göttinger Nachrichten in 1857 and is in the Werke

deep.surprise_reason: This is a bibliographic or archival label for a document already known and published (Riemann's self-announcement of his 1857 hypergeometric memoir). It contains no mathematics.

checkable.sympy: a,b,c,x=symbols('a b c x'); F=hyper([a,b],[c],x); simplify(hyperexpand(x*(1-x)*diff(F,x,2)+(c-(a+b+1)*x)*diff(F,x)-a*b*F))  # expect 0
checkable.asserts: Gauss's series F(α,β,γ,x) satisfies the hypergeometric differential equation (background to the memoir named on the page, not written on it).
The exponents of the hypergeometric equation at 0, 1 and ∞ (0, 1-γ; 0, γ-α-β; α, β) sum to 1. This is the Fuchs relation underlying Riemann's P-function (background, not on the page).
